chunks: And he said in another section:

“For one upon whom God’s favor is great, the proof is multiplied against him, and truthfulness is incumbent upon him in what displeases and pleases him. It is not fitting for me, between me and Allah, but to speak the truth about his matter, despite his great fault. And this man is appointed to a duty from which the elite are not permitted to turn away. And the ruling of Islam, with that, applies to him as it applies to the others among the believers and their mention.”
ai.seo_question: What is the obligation of truthfulness for those with great divine favor according to this text?
ai.summary: This passage from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* underscores the principle of *tadâ'uf al-hujjah* (doubling of the proof), where higher status entails greater accountability for truthfulness in both public and private spheres. It specifically contextualizes the authority of the four deputies (or a specific high-ranking deputy) during the Minor Occultation, affirming that their unique appointment does not exempt them from the general Islamic rulings (*ahkam*) that apply to the broader community of believers.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 360 - In another section, he says,

“Someone upon whom the favors of God are great, many proofs bind him and he must speak the truth in what hurts and what pleases him. It is not permissible for me, between me and Allah, but to speak the truth about this man. This man is appointed to a duty from which the public are not allowed to turn away. The command of Islam applies to him like it was applied to other believers.”
